title: The Owl Atlas — Pi-style and later Old Style image research
status: Specific specimens identified; six full-size image links visually verified in research browser. Reuse review pending. Existing atlas unchanged.
rights_note: The individual Wikimedia Commons file pages carry a PD-France public-domain assertion. specimens.title: Pi III · Athena’s helmet, in detail
specimens.type: Pi III, as catalogued by BnF
specimens.institution: Bibliothèque nationale de France, département Monnaies, médailles et antiques
specimens.collection_reference: SNG France 1, Collection Jean et Marie Delepierre, no. 1475
specimens.catalogue_date: c. 353–295 BCE (BnF catalogue, attributed there to Flament)
specimens.editorial_date: Mid–late fourth century BCE; keep the source’s dating convention visible.
specimens.date_note: This is the specimen catalogue’s date range, not an exact issue date and not a claim that all Pi-style chronology is settled.
specimens.look: The full obverse preserves Athena’s profile eye and the helmet ornament. The reverse gives a separate, close view of the owl and surrounding details. Identification comes from the catalogue, not from appearance alone.

specimens.title: Quadridigité · A named later Old Style group
specimens.institution: Bibliothèque nationale de France, département Monnaies, médailles et antiques
specimens.collection_reference: SNG France 1, Collection Jean et Marie Delepierre, no. 1478
specimens.catalogue_date: c. 286–261 BCE (BnF catalogue, attributed there to Flament)
specimens.editorial_date: Third century BCE; identify this specifically as quadridigité, not as a stand-in for every later Old Style issue.
specimens.date_note: The source’s date convention is preserved. Other specialist catalogues may draw different endpoints.
specimens.look: Both faces are available as full photographs. Compare the helmet treatment with the Pi III example, while retaining the named catalogue classification. This specimen illustrates one later Old Style group, not the whole third century.

specimens.title: Pi II · An additional securely catalogued example
specimens.type: Pi II, as catalogued by BnF
specimens.institution: Bibliothèque nationale de France, département Monnaies, médailles et antiques
specimens.collection_reference: SNG France 1, Collection Jean et Marie Delepierre, no. 1469
specimens.catalogue_date: c. 393–295 BCE (broad BnF catalogue range, attributed there to Flament)
specimens.editorial_date: Pi II; specimen chronology requires reconciliation before a narrow date is assigned.
specimens.date_note: Do not silently turn the broad 393–295 BCE record range into the date of Pi II as a whole. The type identification and the chronology should be stored separately.
specimens.look: The obverse offers another detailed view of the helmet and profile eye. Surface marks remain visible: the image has not been “cleaned up” to make an idealized coin.
